$comment: Vendored dependency manifest (ADR 0021). tools/repo/vendor.luau imports each dependency at the pinned commit and re-applies patches/. Rows below carry the TARGET versions; the 'commit' fields are filled with real SHAs at vendor time (the first import) and THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md is regenerated in the same commit. Adding/upgrading a dependency requires a maintainer-approved ADR (rule R5).
$comment_binaries: ADR 0032 amends ADR 0021 with a second row kind. A row with "kind": "binary" is NOT a source tree: it is a build-time release artifact, fetched at configure time into a cache under $ENG_BUILD_ROOT and pinned by SHA256 per platform, never committed. The hash IS the pin -- a mismatch is a hard configure error, and changing one is a human edit here, exactly as changing a commit SHA is. This exists for artifacts whose source form is disproportionate to their role (DXC's source is a fork of LLVM); anything the engine links is still vendored as source.
$comment_toolchains: ADR 0091 adds a third row kind. A row under "toolchains" is a tool built FROM SOURCE by tools/repo/toolchain.luau, outside the repository (under $ENG_BUILD_ROOT), at a pinned commit whose submodules are pinned too -- git's own hashes are the pin, and the tool refuses a checkout that does not match every one. It is never vendored and never committed. Unlike a binary row it IS redistributed: `redistributed` says so, and the editor package carries its build and its licence texts.

binaries.name: dxc
binaries.note: The HLSL front-end SDL_shadercross needs (ADR 0006), for the ENGINE's own shaders at the engine's own build. Never redistributed: the editor ships the source-built compiler in the toolchains row below instead (ADR 0091). Not vendored and not committed: see ADR 0032 -- the archives carry an unassigned Microsoft EULA alongside the NCSA licence their own ReleaseNotes.md names, and 50 MiB of opaque binaries would land in history per version. Hashes below are the ones SDL_shadercross itself pins, verified byte-for-byte against the published release. No macOS artifact exists; Microsoft publishes none.

toolchains.name: dxc
toolchains.note: The compiler the EDITOR ships so a user's surface shader compiles on the user's machine (ADR 0091). Built from source, which carries no Microsoft terms -- only the NCSA licence and the notices ThirdPartyNotices.txt lists -- and emits hashed DXIL that retail D3D12 accepts with no dxil.dll (U-64, confirmed 2026-09-25). Measured: 5 min 23 s on Windows x64 at -j14, 295 s on Linux x64 in the Tier-2 image; dxcompiler is 21 MB on Windows and 37.5 MB on Linux. Built once per version and platform by `lute tools/repo/toolchain.luau build dxc`, and by CI's dxc-source job, which caches it by commit.

dependencies.name: luau
dependencies.note: The one patch routes the `^` operator and its constant folding through `engine_dpow`, the engine's own pow (ADR 0083), because the C runtime's pow rounds differently on each platform and a script's `x ^ y` is on the simulation's path. The engine defines the symbol and links it into Luau.VM and Luau.Compiler.

dependencies.name: sdl3
dependencies.note: Narrowed (ADR 0042) to every upstream path but two files at its root that are instructions for writing tools, which this repository does not carry. Built with its joystick, haptic and HID support; the HID part is SDL's own bundled hidapi (src/hidapi), used under its BSD-style licence (src/hidapi/LICENSE-bsd.txt). Eight local patches. 0001: the D3D12 backend wrote GPU descriptor groups past the end of its descriptor heaps and replaced heaps mid-bind; still present upstream on 2026-09-24. The patch reserves room for a whole draw or dispatch before writing and rebinds every table after a heap replacement. 0002 (ADR 0091): on a lost device, pushing uniform data dereferenced the NULL uniform buffer the pool returned, so a GPU reset crashed the process inside SDL; the patch drops the data instead. 0003: the vertex buffer views kept the previous pipeline's strides when only the pipeline changed, so an instanced run drawn after a draw without instancing read every instance from the first; the patch sets the views again at every pipeline bind; still present upstream on 2026-10-03. 0004: on a lost device, binding a pipeline left its uniform buffer slots NULL and the next draw or dispatch dereferenced them -- the access violation a hosted runner's removed software device ended three test hosts with; the patch binds nothing for a slot with no buffer, so the submit that follows fails and says why; still present upstream on 2026-10-12. 0005: on a lost device whose pool of descriptor heaps was empty, the first draw of a command buffer was handed no heap and read through it -- a race with the frames still in flight, so the same removal ended one run cleanly and killed the next; the patch leaves the command buffer with no heaps and records no draw or dispatch without them; still present upstream on 2026-10-12. 0006: on Windows a file opened for reading only was shared with other readers and nobody else, in SDL_IOFromFile and in the ioring asynchronous read, so for the length of a read the program that makes the file could neither write it nor rename a new one over it; the patch shares write and delete as well for a read-only open, and leaves a file opened for writing as it was. To be sent upstream; drop each when a pinned release carries its fix. 0007 (ADR 0244): SDL's GPU integration with OpenXR, from its development line (pull request 14837, merged 2026-01-30, for 3.6.0, not released), backported onto this release: the device made on the adapter an OpenXR runtime asks for, a session, and swapchains whose images are SDL_GPUTextures, with the OpenXR loader loaded at run time; the Khronos headers it carries (Apache-2.0 OR MIT) come as they are. Drop it when a pinned release carries the integration. 0008 (ADR 0244 §5): 0007 made every image of an OpenXR swapchain a colour target, so a runtime's depth layer had nothing to write into; a swapchain asked for with the depth-stencil usage is now a depth target, on Vulkan and Direct3D 12. Drop it with 0007, or when upstream carries depth swapchains.

dependencies.name: openxr_sdk
dependencies.note: The OpenXR loader (ADR 0244): the library a game that enables XR ships beside it, and the one SDL loads at run time (patch 0007 of sdl3) to reach whichever runtime the headset installed -- on the Quest, Meta's, found as any runtime is. Built here as a shared library from its sources, never through its own CMake project, which builds API layers, tests and a version resource the engine has no use for; its headers are the engine's OpenXR headers too. Narrowed to the loader's tree: the specification and its generator scripts are left out, because the release carries the generated sources. The loader is Apache-2.0 OR MIT; inside src/external it carries jsoncpp (MIT, or public domain where that is recognised), which the loader reads runtime manifests with, and jnipp (MIT) and android-jni-wrappers (BSL-1.0), which only an Android build compiles. Pinned at release-1.1.63 (2026-09-02) rather than the newest, 1.1.65 of 2026-10-16, so the pin has been in others' use first (R5).

dependencies.name: sdl_shadercross
dependencies.note: Has never cut a release: no tags exist at all, so the version is the pinned commit's date (same treatment as stb).

dependencies.name: spirv_cross
dependencies.note: Pinned at the revision SDL_shadercross's own submodule points to, which is what upstream CI tests against. Required unconditionally by its CMakeLists.txt:145-158; there is no build without it.

dependencies.name: jolt
dependencies.note: Vendored with the physics work, the milestone that first needs it -- the row and its version have existed since planning (ADR 0007) and the roadmap permits vendoring lazily provided the row does, which is the xxhash and meshoptimizer rule. The commit is the v5.6.0 tag, read off upstream with `vendor.luau resolve` rather than recalled.

dependencies.name: box2d
dependencies.note: Vendored with the 2D layer, which first needs it (ADR 0008 committed the version at planning; the maintainer opened the phase on 2026-09-23). The commit is the v3.1.1 tag, read off upstream with `vendor.luau resolve` rather than recalled. **Narrowed by the include list (ADR 0042)**: the library is `include/` and `src/`; the samples application, its fonts and its bundled GLFW/imgui/glad, the benchmark data and the unit-test runner are an application we do not build. Compiled by `third_party/CMakeLists.txt` from its sources directly, not through upstream CMake, which configures the samples by default.

dependencies.name: miniaudio
dependencies.note: Vendored with the input and UI work, the milestone that first needs it -- the row and its version have existed since planning (ADR 0009) and the roadmap permits vendoring lazily provided the row does, which is the xxhash, meshoptimizer and Jolt rule. The commit is the 0.11.25 tag, read off upstream with `vendor.luau resolve` rather than recalled. Of the extras/ tree two files are compiled beside miniaudio.h: extras/stb_vorbis.c (stb_vorbis 1.22, Sean Barrett, public domain or MIT at the reader's choice -- the decoder miniaudio decodes Ogg Vorbis through and does without when it is absent, compiled) and extras/nodes/ma_reverb_node/verblib.h (the reverb); the rest of extras/ and the research/ tree are carried for reference.

dependencies.name: fastgltf
dependencies.note: Requires simdjson unconditionally (CMakeLists.txt:77-82) and downloads it unpinned into deps/ when no simdjson::simdjson target exists. We define that target first and the patch turns the download branch into a FATAL_ERROR -- ADR 0036.

dependencies.name: simdjson
dependencies.note: fastgltf's mandatory dependency (ADR 0036), pinned at the version its own CMake targets -- the same rule the spirv_cross row follows. Only singleheader/simdjson.{h,cpp} is compiled; the pair is committed upstream and is exactly what fastgltf would otherwise fetch.

dependencies.name: basis_universal
dependencies.note: Vendored with the streaming work, the milestone that first needs a texture pipeline (ADR 0010). Two targets rather than one: the TRANSCODER (transcoder/basisu_transcoder.cpp) is linked into the runtime, and the ENCODER (encoder/*.cpp) only into the offline `assetc` tool -- the engine must never be able to write a texture. Encoder settings are pinned to standardized UASTC/ETC1S; XUASTC was still not standardized in early 2026, and a non-portable texture format is the last thing an asset pipeline should reach for. The KTX-Software row beside this one stays unpinned: basis writes and reads the KTX2 container itself, so the pairing partner would be a large tree with its own dependency set bought for a format both halves of which are already here. **Narrowed by the include list (ADR 0042)**: upstream's tree at this commit is 302 MB, of which 275 MB is test images, prebuilt binaries, WebGL demos and Python wheels that nothing here compiles -- and 49 MB of it is exactly the opaque binaries ADR 0032 exists to keep out of history. The nine paths listed are checked out by git pathspec, so what lands is still byte-exact upstream at the pinned commit; what is given up is the whole-tree rule.

dependencies.name: stb
dependencies.note: stb has no tags; version is the pinned commit's date. tests/oversample/oversample.exe is a prebuilt binary upstream's own .gitignore ignores, so it is untracked there and never checked out here -- the tree is byte-exact upstream, and that file's absence is upstream's decision rather than a deviation of ours.

dependencies.name: imgui
dependencies.note: The docking branch, per ADR 0011. Byte-exact upstream, which this note previously claimed it was not: it described excluding examples/libs/glfw/lib-vc2010-{32,64}/glfw3.lib, and those files have been tracked here with the bootstrap. The tree is upstream's tracked files by construction (ADR 0021) and the note is now what the repository actually contains. examples/example_android_opengl3/android/gradle/ is absent because upstream's own nested .gitignore leaves it untracked, not because we exclude it. Only core/ and backends/{sdl3,sdlgpu3} are compiled; the examples/ tree is carried for reference only.

dependencies.name: recastnavigation
dependencies.note: Vendored with the streaming work with the seam only (ADR 0022) and **integrated by ADR 0089**: `engine/nav` builds a tiled navmesh with Recast and answers from it with Detour, and `third_party/CMakeLists.txt` compiles Recast, Detour and -- since ADR 0098's crowds -- DetourCrowd (DetourTileCache stays on disk, unbuilt, until something calls it). **Narrowed by the include list (ADR 0042)**: RecastDemo alone carries SDL, bundled fonts and sample meshes for an application we do not build, and `Tests` pulls Catch2 -- a second test framework in a repository that pins doctest (R5). The four library directories are the library.

dependencies.name: gamenetworkingsockets
dependencies.note: Not vendored, and this note is the reason rather than the absence of one (maintainer's decision, 2026-08-21; still so). ADR 0012 named GNS as the default transport behind `ITransport` and ENet as the alternative. GNS depends on OpenSSL-or-libsodium PLUS protobuf: protobuf is a code generator that invades the build and OpenSSL is a compilation problem on every tier. Replication (ADR 0069 onwards), the relay and its hole punching (ADR 0178) were all built on ENet behind `ITransport`, and ADR 0120 chose to encrypt over ENet rather than move to GNS -- so this row stays empty until a record decides otherwise.

dependencies.name: enet
dependencies.note: The one implementation behind `ITransport` (ADR 0012), and what every match runs on: replication (ADR 0069 onwards), the relay and hole punching (ADR 0178). A single C library with no dependencies. UDP with optional reliability and sequencing, and nothing else: no encryption and no authentication of its own. That is stated here because it is a property a caller must know. ADR 0120 decides how a match is encrypted and a player authenticated over it; until that is built, an ENet match is as private as the network it crosses.

dependencies.name: assimp
dependencies.note: Offline importer tool ONLY -- never linked into the runtime (ADR 0010). It is a dependency of `assetc`, and the layering gate plus this note are what keep it there: the engine reads `.lmesh`, a format assimp has never heard of. glTF stays on fastgltf even though assimp can read it, because the runtime pipeline's importer and the exotic-format importer are different jobs and fastgltf is the one the first renderer proved. Configured with a NARROW importer set and every exporter off (third_party/CMakeLists.txt): assimp's default build is about sixty importers, most of them formats nobody has shipped this decade, and each one is compile time plus attack surface on a tool that reads untrusted files. **Narrowed by the include list (ADR 0042)**: upstream's tree is dominated by `test/models`, hundreds of megabytes of sample assets in the exotic formats themselves -- the very binaries ADR 0032 exists to keep out of history, and useless to us because we do not run assimp's own test suite.

dependencies.name: blake3
dependencies.note: Vendored with the streaming work, the milestone that first needs a ContentHash -- the row and its licence have existed since planning (architecture.md section 2) and the roadmap permits vendoring lazily provided the row does, which is the xxhash, meshoptimizer, Jolt and miniaudio rule. Only c/blake3.c, c/blake3_dispatch.c and c/blake3_portable.c are compiled, with BLAKE3_NO_{SSE2,SSE41,AVX2,AVX512} defined: the SIMD paths need per-file compiler flags or assembler, and a content ADDRESS that depended on which instruction set the build machine had would be a cache key that is not a name. The Rust crate and the reference implementation are carried for reference.

dependencies.name: xxhash
dependencies.note: WorldHash is specified as xxh3 (architecture.md §9). Vendored with the kernel, which is the milestone that first needs it -- the manifest row has existed since planning and the bootstrap's scope permits vendoring lazily provided the row does.

dependencies.name: libsodium
dependencies.note: Vendored 2026-10-02, at the latest release tag (1.0.22-RELEASE), on the maintainer's approval recorded in ADR 0120 -- and EARLIER than that record's ledger put it, because the first game made with the engine needed a login: a script had no random number that was not the simulation's, no hash, and nothing meant for a password, and carried its own SHA-256 in Luau. So the first caller is `CryptoService` (ADR 0151) and the second is the one the approval was given for, the sealed transport. One library for both rather than a hand-written SHA-256 now and libsodium later: a primitive nobody here wrote is one nobody here has to defend. **Narrowed by the include list (ADR 0042)** to the library's own sources and its licence: upstream also carries the autotools machinery, per-platform packaging and the test vectors. **Built by a target of ours, not by its configure script** (third_party/CMakeLists.txt says how): every source file, with none of the `HAVE_*` macros that select an instruction set, so each primitive compiles its reference implementation -- the same bytes on every tier, no per-file compiler flags, no assembler. `version.h` is generated into the build tree from upstream's own `version.h.in`, with the numbers read out of upstream's `configure.ac` -- which is carried for that and for nothing else.

dependencies.name: inter
dependencies.note: The engine's DEFAULT TYPEFACE (maintainer's decision, 2026-08-20). One face, not several: a good default plus "bring your own" covers the ground, and three vendored faces are three things to licence, update and explain. Roboto (Apache-2.0) was the alternative if matching this repository's own licence family were worth more than the typeface, and it is not. OFL 1.1 is a permissive licence for R6's purposes -- it allows redistribution and embedding, and its one real condition is that the font not be sold on its own, which nothing here does. It also forbids using the RESERVED FONT NAME on a modified copy; this vendors the file unmodified, which is ADR 0021's rule anyway. **Narrowed by the include list (ADR 0042)**: upstream is a type-design repository -- sources, build tooling, a web specimen site and every previously released binary. What a game engine needs from it is one file and the licence. `InterVariable.ttf` rather than a static instance because upstream ships no static TTF at this tag; stb_truetype reads its default instance, and `engine/ui`'s atlas test asserts the rendered weight is Regular rather than trusting that.

dependencies.name: smaa
dependencies.note: SMAA 1x, the reference implementation by its authors (ADR 0158, the anti-aliasing and upscaling batch the maintainer approved on 2026-10-03). The repository has no tags; the version is the pinned commit's. **Narrowed by the include list (ADR 0042)** to the shader, the two precomputed lookup tables as C arrays, and the licence: upstream also carries a Direct3D demo, the scripts that generate the tables and the same tables as DDS files. The engine's three SMAA passes include `SMAA.hlsl` through `SMAA_CUSTOM_SL`, mapping its texture macros onto the engine's bindings, and upload the two tables once at boot.

dependencies.name: fidelityfx_fsr1
dependencies.note: AMD FidelityFX Super Resolution 1 -- EASU, the edge-adaptive spatial upscale, and RCAS, the sharpening -- as AMD's portable header (ADR 0158). Source, not an SDK binary: the two headers are written for HLSL and GLSL alike and are compiled into the engine's own fragment passes. **Narrowed by the include list (ADR 0042)** to the headers' folder -- the two of them -- and the licence; upstream also carries a sample application and its media. **One patch**: three of `ffx_a.h`'s helpers choose between vectors with `?:`, which HLSL 2021 -- the language the shader compiler speaks -- allows only for a scalar condition; the patch spells them with `select`. The GLSL side of the header is not compiled here and the patched lines are not reached by it.

dependencies.name: fidelityfx_fsr2
dependencies.note: AMD FidelityFX Super Resolution 2 -- the temporal upscaler (ADR 0164, the second delivery ADR 0158 named). Source, not an SDK binary: the algorithm is AMD's portable shader headers, compiled into the engine's own compute passes through a callbacks header of the engine's own, which is the integration point the headers are written for -- AMD's own names its resources by Direct3D register and keeps samplers apart from textures, which the engine's RHI does not. **Narrowed by the include list (ADR 0042)** to the shader headers, the one table the upscale reads (`ffx_fsr2_maximum_bias.h`) and the licence; upstream also carries the C++ runtime with its Direct3D 12 and Vulkan backends, which the engine does not use -- the frame's constants and the order of the passes are written in the renderer, after `ffx_fsr2.cpp` -- and a sample application with its media.

dependencies.name: fidelityfx_sdk
dependencies.note: AMD FidelityFX SDK 1.1.4 -- FSR 3's frame generation (ADR 0165): the frame interpolation and optical flow techniques. Source, not an SDK binary, and of the last release whose frame generation is source: the algorithms are AMD's portable shader headers, compiled into the engine's own compute passes through callbacks headers the engine derives, as FSR 2's are (ADR 0164). **Narrowed by the include list (ADR 0042)** to those two techniques' shader headers, the core headers they include and the licence; upstream also carries every other FidelityFX technique, the C++ runtime with its Direct3D 12 and Vulkan backends, the frame interpolation swap chain -- which replaces the platform's swap chain, and the engine presents through its RHI -- and sample applications with their media. FSR 2 stays its own row at 2.2.1: this SDK's upscaler is another algorithm.
